subject: Cloud Computing
title: GPUs in the Cloud
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: GPUs in the Cloud.

hook.text: Training an AI model can take thousands of GPUs running for weeks. Nobody owns that many GPUs.

buildup.text: Cloud providers rent GPU clusters by the hour. You get supercomputer power without buying one.

discovery.text: NVIDIA GPUs dominate cloud AI. Their H100 chips cost $30,000 each — and there's a global shortage.

twist.text: Cloud GPU demand is so intense that wait times can be months. The shortage reshapes AI competition.

climax.text: Whoever controls GPU cloud supply controls the pace of AI progress. It's the new arms race.

punchline.text: The cloud's hottest resource isn't storage. It's GPU power.

quiz.question: Why are cloud GPUs in such high demand?
options: Training AI models requires massive GPU power that few can own outright
GPUs are the only chips that can connect to the internet
Cloud providers give away GPUs for free to attract customers

details.summary: Cloud GPU instances provide access to powerful graphics processors for machine learning training, inference, video rendering, and scientific computing. Instead of buying expensive GPU hardware, organizations rent GPU capacity by the hour, accessing the latest chips without upfront investment.
details.whyItMatters: GPU cloud instances democratize access to expensive AI hardware. Organizations can train large models without purchasing GPUs that cost tens of thousands of dollars each.
takeaways: Cloud GPUs provide on-demand access to AI-grade hardware
No upfront GPU purchase is required for ML training
GPU instances can scale from a single GPU to clusters of thousands

faq.question: Which GPUs are available in the cloud?
faq.answer: AWS offers NVIDIA A100, H100, and custom Trainium chips. Google Cloud offers A100s and TPUs. Azure provides A100, H100, and AMD MI300X instances. Availability varies by region, and the latest GPUs are often in high demand with waiting lists.

faq.question: Are cloud GPUs cost-effective for AI training?
faq.answer: For intermittent or experimental training, cloud GPUs are much more cost-effective than buying hardware. For continuous training over months, owned hardware may be cheaper. Many organizations use a mix, with cloud GPUs for burst capacity and owned hardware for baseline workloads.
